info.title: tencent/hunyuan-image-3.5
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "tencent/hunyuan-image-3.5", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Tencent Hunyuan Image 3.5 text-to-image on Tencent MPS. The route is text-only: `prompt` is required and reference `images` are refused (see the field), so a valid call carries a prompt and no images.

example.prompt: a serene mountain lake at sunrise, ultra detailed, cinematic lighting

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio as a W:H ratio such as 16:9.

images.description: Reference images, by public https URL. REFUSED on this route: Hunyuan Image 3.5 is launched text-only, so a non-empty `images` is rejected with a 400. MPS fetches a reference image only by a crawler-accessible URL and cannot be handed stripped bytes, so caller images cannot have their EXIF location data removed first; image input is not supported yet. Send a prompt only.

n.description: Number of images to generate. Only 1 is served (the metered quantity).

negative_prompt.description: Text describing what the image should avoid.

output_format.description: Image encoding of the generated output. One of png or jpeg.

prompt.description: The text prompt describing the image to generate. Required: this route is text-only, so a prompt is the only accepted input. Trimmed before it is signed.
prompt.example: a serene mountain lake at sunrise, ultra detailed, cinematic lighting

resolution.description: Output resolution tier, which is also the metered tier. One of 720p, 1080p, 2k or 4k.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Tencent Hunyuan Image 3.5 on Tencent MPS: the terminal `POST /proxy/tencent/mps/aigc/image/query` document (MPS's DescribeAigcImageTask), forwarded unchanged. The operation is submit-and-poll and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `{"Response": {"TaskId": ...}}` handle the underlying CreateAigcImageTask submit answers with.
THE ASSET IS `Response.ImageUrls`, a list of URL STRINGS: read `ImageUrls[]`, the generated images. At least one entry is a non-empty URL on the document Router returns — a `DONE` task with no fetchable URL is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document, so a `200` here always carries at least one image URL. The list can carry more than one entry, so read the entries rather than assuming the first.
The URLs are Tencent's own delivery links and they EXPIRE — MPS documents about 12 hours. Router does not re-host these images onto Comfy storage, so what a caller receives is Tencent's expiring URL rather than a Comfy one — download the asset rather than storing the link.
`Response.Status` is Tencent's own UPPERCASE vocabulary (`WAIT`, `RUN`, `FAIL`, `DONE`), compared without case folding. `DONE` is the one terminal success and the only value this document can carry: `FAIL`, an HTTP-200 body carrying a `Response.Error` and no `Status`, and a budget-exhausted `WAIT`/`RUN` all reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this body. `RequestId` is Tencent's own troubleshooting handle rather than the job id.

ImageUrls.description: The generated images' download URLs. Present and non-empty on the document Router returns; at least one entry is a fetchable URL. Tencent's own links, documented as valid for about 12 hours.

Message.description: Tencent's status message, documented as an empty string when there is no error.

RequestId.description: Tencent's own request identifier, for troubleshooting with Tencent. It is neither the task id nor an asset.

Status.description: Terminal success status. This document is returned only for `DONE`; other MPS statuses reach a Router caller as an error.
